  "text": "Every Tuesday, Arthur took the long way to the swimming pool so he could pass his old house.

He never stopped. He looked at the gate, which needed painting, and the upstairs window where his daughter had once kept a row of jam jars full of coloured water.

In April, the new owner pulled out the rose bushes.

Arthur mentioned it to the woman at the pool desk.

“Perhaps they were diseased,” she said.

“They weren’t.”

The following week, a small boy was digging beside the path. He had a kitchen spoon and an empty ice-cream tub.

“Looking for treasure?” Arthur asked through the gate.

“Making a pond.”

Arthur considered the tub.

“You’ll need stones so things can climb out.”

“What things?”

“Whatever falls in.”

On Tuesday he brought three flat stones in his swimming bag. The boy wasn’t there, so Arthur left them beside the gate.

A week later, they surrounded the tub. A wooden sign said POND. Someone had drawn a fish beneath the word.

The boy’s mother came out carrying a watering can.

“Were those yours?” she asked.

Arthur nodded.

“He’s waiting for frogs.”

“It may take a while.”

“That’s what I said.”

She tipped a little water into the tub. Arthur noticed that one rose remained, cut almost to the ground beneath the window.

“That one smells lovely,” she said. “Do you know what it’s called?”

He told her he would try to remember.

At home, he opened the drawer where they had kept plant labels. There it was, under some string.

He put it in his swimming bag."
